$comment: What each harness gets from plugins/rig. Read by build-lib.sh, the build-*-plugin.sh scripts and install.sh --check. #169 - rig declares and installs every harness's plugins and MCP servers, and reports drift.

claude.$comment: Claude Code, on WSL or native Windows (hooks run under Git Bash there). The plugin loads from the GitHub marketplace as a whole directory, so this target lists everything; nothing is built.

codex.$comment: WSL Codex CLI as an organizer. autopilot crosses: its wake-up is the OS scheduler through scripts/wake.sh. no-comments stays out: it spawns a named Claude subagent.

codex-desktop.$comment: Windows Codex desktop app: a delegated thread that works one packet. Hooks stay out, being bash scripts that read WSL paths.

claude-windows.$comment: Windows Claude Code: no agy, so farm-out, lane and agy-runner stay out, and autopilot with them since it routes lanes through farm-out; no hooks, being bash scripts that read WSL paths.

no-doze.autopilot: the scheduled-tick aside; the skill says what to do without it
no-doze.farm-out: a pointer to a worked kill example; the rule stands without it

agy.$comment: Antigravity CLI, a lane worker first. GEMINI.md is the lane contract; ~/.gemini/AGENTS.md carries the neutral core plus the agy overlay, whose first line gives a lane run's work order precedence.

unshipped.$comment: An artifact in no target must be named here with the reason, or every build fails.
